The claim states that the method should be used when HDR latent values are 'strictly required' and suggests using BCF6 instead. It solves the storage and memory bandwidth bottleneck of high-resolution PBR assets by leveraging existing block compression hardware for random access while using neural inference to reconstruct high-dimensional material properties [S1].

The claim states that the method solves storage and memory bandwidth bottlenecks for high-resolution PBR assets by using existing block compression hardware for random access and neural inference for reconstruction. The evidence supports this in multiple ways: 1) The abstract and introduction explicitly mention mitigating storage capacity costs on disk and VRAM for high-resolution (4096x4096) PBR assets. 2) The notes and Section 3.1 confirm that latent features are stored in BC1 format (block compression) and decoded using hardware texture filtering (random access). 3) Section 3.1 and Figure 1 describe using a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) to reconstruct feature vectors (high-dimensional material properties) from the latent colors. 4) Section 4 and the notes mention using hardware matrix multiplication engines (cooperative vectors) to accelerate the neural inference, addressing performance/bandwidth concerns.
